title: Bills of Lading and Transport Documents: Telex Release Terms by Document Type
content:
This quick-reference card sets out, for every `Bills of Lading and Transport Documents` type, the three tariff terms that govern a telex release: whether the type offers a telex release at all, the fee per telex release in US dollars, and the lowest service contract tier rank at which that fee stops being charged.

## Terms by document type

| Document type | Telex release offered | Telex release fee (USD per release) | Lowest exempting contract tier rank |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Sea Waybill | No | 0.00 | 0 |
| AHL Electronic Bill of Lading | No | 0.00 | 0 |
| AHL Straight Bill of Lading | Yes | 40.00 | 5 |
| AHL Negotiable Bill of Lading | Yes | 55.00 | 5 |
| AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading | Yes | 60.00 | 4 |
| AHL Switch Bill of Lading | Yes | 75.00 | 6 |

## Meaning of the columns

- **Telex release offered** states whether the type can be released at destination on the strength of a full surrender of its originals at the origin office.
- **Telex release fee** is the amount charged for one telex release, in USD per release.
- **Lowest exempting contract tier rank** is the smallest service contract tier rank that frees the release from the fee. A figure of 0 in this column means that no contract, whatever its rank, frees the release from the fee.

## Points of judgement

- The sea waybill and the electronic bill of lading do not offer a telex release; their zero fee and zero rank simply reflect that the service does not exist for them.
- Among the four paper types that offer the service, the combined transport bill has the lowest exemption threshold (rank 4) and the switch bill the highest (rank 6).
- **Hypothetical comparison.** For an AHL Straight Bill of Lading, a contract of rank 4 sits below the threshold of 5 and does not exempt the fee, while a contract of rank 5 or 6 reaches it. For an AHL Combined Transport Bill of Lading, rank 4 already reaches the threshold.
